Found a bug, hit a deployment problem, or want to request a feature? Report it in the repository that owns the relevant component. This page is a lightweight triage map plus where to get help. For security vulnerabilities, do not open a public issue — follow Security policy & reporting instead.

Pick the right repo

Deploy App is spread across separate repos, so the fastest route to a fix is filing against the component that actually owns the behavior.

If the problem is in... File against Notes
The Docker Compose stack / overall legacy deployment, .env, ports, subdomains, miniwerk, CFSSL pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration The legacy "one ring" composition; many components are submodules here.
The Kubernetes deployment, Kustomize bases/overlays, task/mise tooling, cert-manager/trust-manager/PKI wiring pvarki/opendefence-platform The new (alpha) k8s stack.
Core user CRUD, Deploy App login/identity flow, the integration callback API surface pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api The core rmapi — the integration point that product integrations call.
Scaffolding a new product integration (copier template, generated layout) pvarki/python-integration-template The copier template, not a running service.
A specific product integration's behavior The per-product *-rmapi repo e.g. python-matrix-rmapi (Matrix), python-tak-rmapi (TAK), python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz (MediaMTX).

Component to repo (legacy submodules)

If you traced the problem to a submodule directory inside docker-rasenmaeher-integration, file against its upstream repo (from the README "Directories that are submodules"):

  • api → python-rasenmaeher-api (core rmapi)
  • miniwerk → python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk (Let's Encrypt certs, subdomains, MW_PRODUCTS)
  • cfssl → docker-rasenmaeher-cfssl (internal CA)
  • keycloak → docker-keycloak; openldap → docker-openldap
  • uiv2 → react-rasenmaeher-ui-v2
  • takserver → docker-atak-server; takintegration → python-tak-rmapi
  • battlelog → typescript-liveloki-app; mtxauthz → python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz
  • fpintegration → python-rasenmaeher-rmfpapi; kw_product_init → golang-kraftwerk-init-helper-cli

What to include

To make a report actionable:

  • Stack and version — legacy Compose or Kubernetes, and the tag/commit you are on. For the legacy stack include the submodule set (you pin a consistent set via tags — see Releases & versioning).
  • What you did / expected / saw — exact commands, env vars (redact secrets), and the failing output.
  • Logs — relevant container/pod logs. The legacy stack often just needs a re-run on first start ("OpenLDAP and keycloak-init sometimes fail on first start, just run up again"); note if the failure persists.
  • Reproduction — minimal steps; whether it reproduces in a clean environment (legacy integration tests "expect a clean database to start with").

Community & channels

  • GitHub Issues / Discussions on the relevant pvarki repo are the primary channel.
  • For background on what Deploy App is and why, the Disobey24 talk linked from the legacy README is a good orientation.
